Piecewise linear or logistic trends

Source: R/trend_system.R
piecewise_trends.Rd

A trend that grows at a constant rate between changepoints, as in Prophet (Taylor and Letham 2018). Linear growth is unbounded. Logistic growth saturates at a carrying capacity that data supplies. The constructor records its arguments. The model evaluates them against the data.

Usage

PW(
  time = NA,
  series = NA,
  cap = NA,
  n_changepoints = 10,
  changepoint_range = 0.8,
  changepoint_scale = 0.3,
  growth = "linear",
  n_lv = NULL,
  trend_map = NULL
)

Arguments

time

The unquoted name of the numeric or integer variable in data that holds each row's time. Defaults to time.

series

The unquoted name of the factor variable in data that names each row's series. Its levels fix the order of the series. A trend needs this column even for a single series. Defaults to series.

cap

The unquoted name of the variable in data that holds the carrying capacity of a logistic model, on the response scale. It is numeric and can vary by time and series. Defaults to cap. A logistic model whose data lack the column is refused.

n_changepoints

A positive integer: the number of potential changepoints, spaced evenly over the first changepoint_range of the time points in data. Defaults to 10.

changepoint_range

A number in (0, 1]: the share of the series that holds the potential changepoints. The default 0.8 leaves the last fifth with the growth rate of the last changepoint. A changepoint among the final points would be estimated from too few observations to trust in a forecast.

changepoint_scale

A positive number: the typical change in growth at one changepoint over the whole series, in link units for linear growth and in logits for logistic growth. For a series of N time points each per-step rate change takes double_exponential(0, s * changepoint_scale / N), where s is the factor get_prior() describes for linear growth and 1 for logistic growth. Larger values give a more flexible trend. The default 0.3 gives the ten default changepoints a prior median movement of the level of about half a unit over the series, the movement the LLT() slope prior allows. Prophet's default of 0.05 holds a link-scale trend close to a straight line.

growth

'linear' (the default) or 'logistic'.

n_lv, trend_map

Factor models are not supported for PW(). Supplying either is refused.

Value

An object of class mvgam_trend.

Details

Intercepts: A linear trend takes its level from the observation formula, as every other trend in mvgam does. y ~ 1 is its ordinary observation formula.

A logistic trend contributes cap * inv_logit(...) on the link scale. Its offset m_trend places the inflection in time. The expectation saturates at cap when the observation formula omits its intercept (y ~ -1 or y ~ 0 + ...). An intercept raises the ceiling above cap.

Priors: Time runs in steps 1, ..., N. The base growth rate takes k_trend ~ normal(0, 2 s / (N - 1)), two units of growth over the series at one standard deviation. The logistic inflection takes m_trend ~ normal((N + 1) / 2, N / 2), centred on the middle of the series. get_prior() shows the values for a given model.

The carrying capacity: A market size, a population size or an ecological carrying capacity can bound a series. growth = 'logistic' takes it from the cap column, which can vary by series and by time. Every observation needs a value. Under a non-identity link the capacity is moved to the link scale, such as its log under poisson() or negbinomial(). Give it on the scale of the response.

References

Taylor, S. J. and Letham, B. (2018). Forecasting at scale. The American Statistician, 72, 37-45. doi:10.1080/00031305.2017.1380080

See also

LLT() for a trend whose growth changes continuously. get_prior() lists the default priors. The forecast evaluation article compares a piecewise trend with other trends out of sample.

Other trend models: LLT(), RW(), ZMVN(), list_trend_types(), lv_axis()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(2024)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                     n_timepoints = 120L)
mod <- mvgam(
  y ~ 1,
  trend_formula = ~ PW(growth = "linear"),
  data          = simdat$data_train,
  family        = poisson(),
  chains        = 2,
  silent        = 2
)
summary(mod)
#>  Family: poisson 
#>   Links: mu = log 
#> Formula: y ~ 1 
#>    Data: simdat$data_train (Number of observations: 90) 
#>  Trends: PW(linear)

#>          total post-warmup draws = 2000
